# OpenAPI Contracts — RealityEngine

Seven OpenAPI 3.1.0 documents describe the HTTP surfaces: RE and PE for each
runtime, plus the Manager's external API. All seven are **generated** — do not
edit them by hand. Edit the source files and regenerate.

## Generated files

| File | Runtime | Service | Default port |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`cpp-re.yaml`](cpp-re.yaml) | CPP (C++ / Boost.Beast) | Reality Engine  | `5301` |
| [`cpp-pe.yaml`](cpp-pe.yaml) | CPP (C++ / Boost.Beast) | Perception Engine | `5300` |
| [`lsp-re.yaml`](lsp-re.yaml) | LSP (SBCL / Hunchentoot) | Reality Engine  | `5601` |
| [`lsp-pe.yaml`](lsp-pe.yaml) | LSP (SBCL / Hunchentoot) | Perception Engine | `5600` |
| [`scala-re.yaml`](scala-re.yaml) | Scala (Akka-HTTP) | Reality Engine  | `5001` |
| [`scala-pe.yaml`](scala-pe.yaml) | Scala (Akka-HTTP) | Perception Engine | `5000` |
| [`manager.yaml`](manager.yaml) | — | Manager (external API) | `3001` |

The first six describe the **internal** surface — reached by addressing one
engine's port and answered by whichever engine you reached. `manager.yaml`
describes the **external** one, where the engine is part of the address
(`/api/engine/:id/…`), because vector, sequence and control values are scoped to
the runtime holding them (#397, #401).

## Not generated, and not part of this set

| File | |
|---|---|
| `reality-engine.yaml`, `perception-engine.yaml` | RealityEngine AI — the retired TypeScript prototype, outside the focus set. OpenAPI **3.0.3**, hand-maintained, regenerated by nothing. `RELEASE.md` excludes them from the release set. |

They are named for what they described and sit beside the generated documents,
which reads as a canonical pair unless you open them. Leave them alone or delete
them; do not treat them as stale copies of `cpp-re.yaml` and `cpp-pe.yaml`.

## Source files

| Source | Role |
|---|---|
| `RealityEngine_CI/SURFACE_SPEC.md` | Canonical route authority — every path and method. The master lives here; the runtime repositories hold pointers to it, which `scripts/check-surface-specs.sh` enforces. |
| `scripts/openapi/overlays/{cpp,lsp,scala}.yaml` | Runtime overlays — `info.title`, `info.version`, `servers` |
| `scripts/openapi/generate.py` | Generator — parses SURFACE_SPEC.md, applies overlay, writes YAML |
| `scripts/openapi/validate.py` | Validator — checks a document against the OpenAPI specification |

## Validation

```bash
python3 scripts/openapi/validate.py docs/openapi/*.yaml
bash scripts/tests/test-openapi-validate.sh     # the validator's own tests
```

`audit-docs.sh` check 3 runs both halves: the documents are **current** with
SURFACE_SPEC, and they are **valid OpenAPI**. The second half exists because the
first compares generated output against generated output — a generator emitting
an invalid document compares equal to itself and passes. Three defects lived in
this directory under the currency check alone (#403).

## Regenerate

```bash
# From RealityEngine_CI root:
bash scripts/generate-openapi.sh

# Also copy into each runtime's docs/openapi/:
bash scripts/generate-openapi.sh --propagate
```

Requires Python 3 with `pyyaml` (`pip3 install pyyaml`).

## Quick view

### Swagger portal (all six specs, no Docker)

[`index.html`](index.html) is a self-contained Swagger UI portal with a
runtime + service dropdown over the six per-runtime specs. Serve it (and the sibling
`.yaml` files) over plain HTTP:

```bash
# From RealityEngine_CI root:
bash scripts/serve-openapi.sh          # -> http://localhost:8088
npm run openapi:serve                  # same thing
```

Then open <http://localhost:8088/>. The selection is reflected in the
querystring (e.g. `?runtime=scala&service=pe`) so individual views are
linkable.

When served through `scripts/serve-openapi.sh`, the checked-in generated specs
are exposed with a runtime-aware `servers:` block that points to the same-origin
Swagger proxy:

```text
http://localhost:8088/proxy/{cpp,lsp,scala}/{re,pe}
```

The proxy resolves live targets from `/tmp/re-registry/re-registry.json`, so
"Try it out" follows the active universe instead of static local ports. The
generated YAML files remain the source artifacts and should not be edited by
hand.

### Alternatives

```bash
# Redocly CLI
npx @redocly/cli preview-docs docs/openapi/cpp-re.yaml

# Swagger UI (Docker) — single spec
docker run -p 8081:8080 \
  -e SWAGGER_JSON=/spec/cpp-re.yaml \
  -v $PWD/docs/openapi:/spec \
  swaggerapi/swagger-ui
# open http://localhost:8081
```

> The MCP gateway (`mcp/`) packages the same RE/PE surfaces as Model Context
> Protocol tools for ecosystem integration. See [`../../mcp/README.md`](../../mcp/README.md).

## Code generation

```bash
npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate \
  -i docs/openapi/cpp-re.yaml \
  -g typescript-axios \
  -o generated/cpp-re-client
```

## Path coverage

The generator reads every route table in `SURFACE_SPEC.md` and emits one
operation per `METHOD + path` combination. Rather than quote counts that go
stale between edits — these said 59 and 40 against an actual 65 and 41 — read
them from the documents:

```bash
python3 scripts/openapi/validate.py docs/openapi/*.yaml   # prints paths per document
```

Operation summaries, request-body schemas, and response schemas are sourced
from a catalogue in `generate.py`. Paths not in the catalogue receive a
documented skeleton with `additionalProperties: true` schemas.
